result.title: Exploring the Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Single-Pair Generator Biases in Direct Preference Optimization
result.summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) typically relies on preference pairs generated from diverse model pools and ranked by an external LLM judge. The recently proposed delta-learning hypothesis suggests that comparable supervision can instead be obtained from a single pair of models by treating the larger model's response as preferred. We investigate the limits of this approach across model families and scales. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that fixed model pairs introduce systematic, generator-dependent biases that are predictive of the preference label independent of response quality. Consequently, DPO trained on single-pair data consistently underperforms multi-model preference data, despite the larger generator producing higher-quality responses, and we trace this gap to training dynamics consistent with reward hacking on these biases. We further show that simply increasing the number of generators, even without an external judge, is enough to partially mitigate this effect. Our results highlight generator diversity as a critical factor in preference-data construction.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文检验「delta learning」假设的边界：仅用一对大小模型、以大模型回答作为偏好样本构造 DPO 数据。作者从理论与实验上说明固定模型对会引入与回答质量无关、由生成器决定的系统性偏好偏差，导致 DPO 效果不及多模型偏好数据，并归因于对这些偏差的 reward hacking；增加生成器数量可在无外部评判者时部分缓解。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「监督信号由生成器身份而非内容质量决定、并诱发 reward hacking」的结论，可供核查以模型输出或更强模型轨迹作为正例来训练 VLM 推理轨迹时，标签优势是否实际来自内容贡献。
